dedupe_keys.name: heidelberg university hospital full scale mass casualty exercise with geotracking of 91 simulated casualties 2026

description: This case study reports a full-scale mass casualty exercise at Heidelberg University Hospital in Germany that measured hospital performance objectively instead of relying only on observers. Staff handled 91 simulated casualties through a two-stage triage process while both patients and staff wore location tags, so every movement and contact was tracked. Triage was correct for 75.4 percent of patients, with about one in ten of the most serious cases undertriaged; triage took about one minute for red, three for yellow and three and a half for green patients. Tracking showed steady patient flow without bottlenecks and about seven patient contacts per staff member, and questionnaires found high time pressure but good teamwork, with experienced staff reporting less workload. The article is free to read and download as open access under CC BY in BMC Emergency Medicine (2026). Coverage is one exercise at one German university hospital. Caveats: a single exercise with simulated patients; the tracking data are not stated as available, and facts here come from the abstract. Simulation uses: triage times, error rates and staff contact rates to calibrate hospital surge and patient flow models for mass casualty events. Related records: the Tuscany emergency department study (case_study-tuscany-emergency-department-seismic-resilience) models waiting times after an earthquake, a related measure of emergency department performance.

name: Heidelberg University Hospital: full-scale mass casualty exercise with geotracking of 91 simulated casualties (2026)
organisations: Medical Faculty Heidelberg, Department of Anesthesiology
outcomes: Overall triage accuracy 75.4%; undertriage 11.6% in category I and 10.1% in category II, overtriage 2.9%; mean triage times 59 s (red), 173 s (yellow) and 205 s (green); no patient flow bottlenecks detected; 7.1 patient contacts per staff member; NASA-TLX workload 66.7; TEAM ratings 79.8%.
provider: von der Forst, Schaefer, Mohr and colleagues, Department of Anesthesiology, Heidelberg University (BMC Emergency Medicine, 2026)
resources_used: Location tags on patients and staff for continuous spatiotemporal tracking
